half: BEFORE — current prompt shape, prior to any reordering in reckon prompts.py
method: Byte-level shared prefix computed directly from the dispatched prompt files. NOT an endpoint replay: a 12KB prompt is ~88 block queries against ~1.16M ambient queries per 45s window (0.0076%), so a delta measurement would read noise, not cache. This method is exact, needs no endpoint, is immune to residual cache from the original dispatches, and is reproducible byte-identically after the fix.
why_this_is_the_right_quantity: vLLM prefix caching matches blocks from position 0 while bytes are identical, so shared_prefix_bytes bounds the achievable cross-worker hit fraction on a first turn. The engine-side rate follows mechanically from this number.
refutation: After the fix, this same computation on fresh prompts must show a materially larger shared prefix. No movement refutes the placement hypothesis.
why_replay_was_not_run: Two independent reasons, both verified rather than assumed. (1) Signal: a 12KB prompt is ~88 block queries against ~1.16M ambient queries per 45s window, 0.0076%. (2) No instrument: the engine returns prompt_tokens_details=null, so there is no per-request cached-token count with which to isolate one request from fleet traffic. The incremental B-given-A framing addresses cache contamination but not signal-to-noise, so it does not rescue the method. This byte measurement is the controlled arm instead — same prompts, one variable, and deterministic rather than stochastic.

cohort_half.status: authorised by reckon's operator; dispatch window to follow
cohort_half.size: n=2-3, real owed nodes rather than synthetic traffic
cohort_half.power: INDICATIVE, NOT POWERED — hold it as such
cohort_half.confound: before and after cohorts do DIFFERENT work, because the owed nodes will have been done by then. The cohort measures multi-turn behaviour under real conditions; it is NOT a controlled comparison and must not be written up as one.
cohort_half.parallelism: worker prompts are composed at dispatch, so once the before-cohort is dispatched its prompts are fixed under the current shape and a later prompts.py change cannot contaminate them. Only the AFTER cohort must wait for the merge.

after_half_validity_condition: CRITICAL — the after-cohort must be dispatched by a coordinator process RESTARTED after the merge, not merely dispatched after the merge landed. Measured 2026-09-15: two prompts dispatched 7 and 16 seconds after commit 59526eb still showed 152 B shared with the node id as first divergence, because the dispatching process had already imported the old prompts.py. A running process does not pick up a merge. Applying the refutation condition to such prompts yields a FALSE NEGATIVE that looks exactly like a refuted hypothesis. Verify the divergence point, not only the file mtime.
baseline_reproduced: 152 B reproduced on two further prompts from a third dispatch window (r-20260915T0906*), so the before figure rests on five prompts across three windows and two projects rather than three prompts from one.
